instructions: Take the dough balls out of the fridge and leave them on the counter, covered, for 30 minutes. Set a pizza stone or steel on the rack in the upper third of the oven. A heavy baking sheet turned upside down works too.
Heat the oven to 500°F (260°C). Give a stone or steel 45 minutes, or a baking sheet 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, crush 1 cup of the tomatoes by hand in a bowl, leaving some chunks. Stir in the salt.
Slice the garlic as thin as you can.
Flour a rimless baking sheet or a pizza peel. Stretch one dough ball with your hands into a 12 inch circle, with the middle thin and the rim slightly thicker. Set it on the floured sheet.
Spread half of the tomato mixture over the dough, stopping a little short of the rim. Scatter on half of the garlic, then 3/4 tsp of the oregano. Drizzle on 2 tbsp of the oil.
Slide the pizza onto the hot stone. Bake for 7 to 10 minutes, until the edge is puffed and lightly charred in spots.
Let it rest for 30 seconds, then slice. Make the second pizza the same way.
Taste a slice. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt and a little more oil.
method_notes: Coley Cooks (the lead, no ratings) and Ooni both build a pizza marinara from stretched dough, hand-crushed tomatoes, sliced garlic, dried oregano and olive oil, with no cheese. Ooni adds fresh basil and bakes in a very hot oven for 1 to 2 minutes; Coley Cooks bakes at 500°F for 7 to 10 minutes, which suits a home oven. Store-bought dough makes it quick but not a 30 minute dinner, since the oven needs to heat and the dough needs to sit out. Check the dough label if you need it to be dairy-free and vegan.
